We need the phone." My husband said then, "I'll deal with this person." And the police said, "Well, in that case, we'll organise a patrol." That's what they did when they were concerned, but when we were concerned, it didn't matter. That's how things happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did you hear about people receiving similar threats over the telephone or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Who were these people? What ethnicity were these people?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: All the Croats and the Hungarians, all the Croats. There were some good Serbs, too, some very good ones. I'd single out some of the good ones, the best ones. A lot of time has passed, but there was the head of the school, Trifunovic, and there was Dobroslav Markovic. He is married to a Croat, but this didn't mean anything to him. He was an exceptionally good man. And there were others. I'll repeat what I have said. You just can't imagine how beautiful the relationship was between members of all ethnic groups. This isn't something one taught our children. We didn't teach our children that someone was a Hungarian, while others were Serbs and so on. I'm partly a Hungarian, my mother is a Hungarian. But as far as the Serbs are concerned, my -- all the same, are also baptized a Serbian child. We had lunch in each other's houses. We would celebrate festivities. They would come and celebrate Easter and Christmas with us, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Were some people targeted more than others, and for which reason if "yes"?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: You say that they were looking for big houses, not for small houses. Were the most healthy people, people in the village, targeted with these threats more than other people?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Correct, that's certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did you speak with the Serb refugees? How did they describe the reason for arriving in Hrtkovci?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I'll just give you an example. Someone came to the shop. Sometimes my husband would replace me. As I'm a woman, I would have to do my duties as a woman. He replaced me, and he asked the gentleman why he had come there, what the reason was. And he said "Well, because they have promised us that this will be Serbia, that it will all be ours." And my son doesn't want to learn Cyrillic -- rather, I apologise, doesn't want to learn the Latin script. My son wants to learn to write by using the Cyrillic script, not the Latin script.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: You say that some of these events happened before the arrival of Vojislav Seselj in Hrtkovci. Did you attend the rally on the 6th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I'm a curious being. I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Why did you go there?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, look, I was curious. I wanted to see what this man wanted. I don't know whether you can understand this. Everything was wonderful and peaceful, and now someone wants to destroy this. Why? Well, let's see why, let's hear what the reason is for this. In the morning, I opened up my shop. Since I was to work the first shift, I opened the shop. Well, it's difficult for me to be precise. I'm a woman, so I can't be very precise, you know. But about 300 metres from my house, there's a road, and they had constructed a kind of stage by using tractor-trailers. I don't know whether you can imagine this, but that was the stage. They started singing Serbian songs, which I hadn't heard before. So these songs were being sung. I was somewhat surprised. Why were they suddenly singing these songs? We couldn't understand this. Very briefly, we didn't understand that such things would happen. They started singing Serbian songs. Initially, I didn't want to go there. What does he want, what's he playing at now, what's he up to, et cetera; so that's how I reacted. And then in the end, out of curiosity, I said, "To hell with it, I'm going to go and see what he has to say."

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Was anyone escorting or accompanying Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, when I came close to the stage, I heard huge applause, and I told myself, ah, there he is, he's arrived. He was already on the stage. Around him, to his left, to his right, there were people. He was not alone on the stage. And as I was coming closer and closer to him, I was horrified, because I was seeing in the flesh what I had never seen before. And I must say it was horrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I saw his army. Those were people, his troops, all in black, black like this frame of this monitor, dressed in black from head to toe. They had ammunition belts across their chests, hanging from one shoulder and another. They had rifles. Of course, I can't tell you the type of rifle, because I don't know anything about that. They had Serbian-style traditional peasant hats, and they had something I saw for the first time in my life; and it was horrific to me, those cockades on their caps. And from those hats and cockades, I knew it was the Serbian Army. I knew it was not the regular army, because I recognised the regular army. And to me, those people were frightening, horrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: You say that Seselj was not alone on the stage. Did you recognise anybody who was on the stage with Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that person who said his son shall not learn the Latinic script. His name was Zelic. I knew him, and this Zelic was standing to the left of Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: He's the same man that came to your shop; am I right?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, because he was close to the house. His parents had taken over one house that was close to mine, and he came there often.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: So when you arrived, Mr. Seselj had already begun his speech, because you say that you heard an applause?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: There was a speech, and then he began.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can you describe, to the best of your recollection, exactly what Mr. Seselj said in his speech?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, the first thing he said, and it was strange to me that he was addressing only to brother Serbs and sister Serbs - that was not the usual way people addressed the locals. We use the old-fashioned way, "Hello, comrades." And as long as he was saying "brother and sister Serbs," there must have been an intention behind it. As to what he said, he issued threats that we had to leave. Then he was talking about politics again, that we had to leave, we had to free up the jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: When you say "we," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: We, we who have jobs, we Croats. We Croats, at the end of the day, Croats and some Hungarians.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Please continue with a description of the speech.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: That we had to go, that we had to vacate our jobs, that these people who had newly arrived needed houses. The houses had to accommodate these new people, and that we should not reckon on coming back, that we had to go, that buses would be organised; and we would go on these buses up to the border, we Croats and Hungarians, but mostly Croats. And from the border, we would have to walk. And I'm quoting his words. We would go on buses. We, the Croats and Hungarians, would go on buses, and the new authority "will be us." And then he pounded his chest. I saw many surprised faces in the public, including some Serbs. I stress "some." And among the decorative trees, children were hiding, clapping, and shouting, "Ustashas will drive you out, Ustashas will drive you out." Those were the words of the audience who attended that rally.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Do you remember if, during this speech, was anybody named?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The people named were those holding some sort of prominent position; one doctor, then Mato Sama, who was a manager; Mr. Grizelj, director of the cooperative; Franjo Maricic, who worked in the local commune; and other people who had good jobs and high positions were named. They were named as people who had to leave their jobs, that's what Seselj said, because the people who had newly arrived from Croatia had to have those jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Was any of your relatives named?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Franja Baricevic was one of those named, and he's my brother. And the Barisic who worked in the local commune was also named.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: What was his position [French interpretation on English channel]?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Franjo was in charge of the hydrants and the water supply in the village. He worked in the local commune. He was an employee of the local commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did he give -- Mr. Seselj give a reason for why those people had to leave Hrtkovci, or the Croats had to leave Hrtkovci?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: He said those people had to leave so that he could place his own people, so that they would have jobs. Of course, these people needed the jobs of those who were already in those positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: These people who were mentioned, were they only Croats or non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: They were Croats, down to the last one, Croats and Hungarians. Franjo was half Hungarian. Another person was Hungarian. Yes, mainly Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Those people mentioned during the speech, did they later, subsequently, experience any hostility or maltreatment?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, depends on what you mean by "hostility." If there had been no pressure, of course these people wouldn't have left their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: So you already described the audience response to Seselj's speech. Can you tell us which word or phrases generated this kind of response, an enthusiastic response by the crowd?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, the audience responded most enthusiastically when he said the Croats would be boarded on buses, and he, Seselj, he said that pounding his chest, would be the government. He didn't say that he, himself, would be the new authority, but he said "we." And he knows best whom he meant. That's when he got the greatest applause from the audience. That's when the greatest commotion occurred, and the shouts, "Ustashas, Ustashas." I don't know why, but that's how they called us. What can we do about it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did you recognise anyone in the audience, and did you discuss the speech with this person?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. That's why I didn't hear all of what he said. I could have listened more carefully. But from his party, there was Milena Rajakovic. Her parents lived close to my house. She stood next to me to hear what I was going to say. My employee was also standing next to me because my husband had let her attend the rally instead of working, and there were also some of my other neighbours who were Croats, whereas she was Serb. So I talked to her. I talked perhaps too much, and she remembered.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: What did she say?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, she was in favour of her own party, and I was against it. I was saying: "Why would Seselj be allowed to come here now? Why would he drive me out? I didn't do anything wrong. He had no reason to drive me out." And then I said at the end -- perhaps it's a bit ridiculous, but I said, "It's my house, I've just built it. For someone to just take it away from me, I wouldn't allow. I'll take a bottle of gas and blow up somebody else's house." What I said might be ridiculous, but I was so distraught and disappointed, I hope you can understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: How do you know that this Milena Rajakovic was a member of the Seselj party?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Because she -- because I knew her well, and she was constantly in contact with Ostoja Sibincic, and Ostoja Sibincic was the main man in Hrtkovci, who organised it all and who made a list of all the names of owners of the best houses. He knew that, because he had been brought to our village from Slavonia. They got the house of -- that formerly belonged to some Germans, so it was practically through colonization that his family got the house they lived in.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: You say there was a list of all the names of the owners of the best houses. Did you see this list?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I didn't see it, myself, but you don't have to see a list for yourself if people are being chased out one by one, this house, that house, and then the next one. People who had nothing, no house, no land, were not persecuted; but if it went the way it did, it meant the persecution targeted those who were wealthy and had large houses. If somebody is going after you, you'll easily understand that it's you because you have a large house, whereas I won't be affected because I have nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: How long did the speech last?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: You mean Seselj's speech or all the speeches? There had been speeches before Seselj that I did not attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Seselj's.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Seselj's speech went on easily for an hour, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: At the end of the day, what message did you get from this speech?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: What do you mean, "message"? The message was, "You can't survive here. Get out here -- get out of here, save your skin and that of your family, any way you know how." The message was that we Croats and Hungarians had to get out of that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Was there a change in Hrtkovci, after this speech, in the relationship among the different groups?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: After that, people were very intimidated, frightened, didn't feel like working anymore. We didn't have our hearts in it. Our houses were taken over, and a kind of unrest overwhelmed the village. The hardworking people didn't -- couldn't work anymore. Everyone only thought of surviving from one day to the next, and waiting for what would come next.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I can, of course I can. After this speech he made and that rally, a lady came to visit us with her son aged 16. She spent ten days in our house. Until then, the police had no need to call on us. I had to give her my new bedroom with the new furniture that my father had bought us as a house-warming present. She slept in my room, together with her son. She cooked on my stove, helped herself to the meat from my fridge. When I had come back from the church, I found her eating lunch with her son. She was beside herself with happiness. She couldn't believe her good luck in getting our house. She didn't think twice about saying to her son, "God, can it really be true that we got a house like this?" She already thought of it as her house, and she thought that we had to leave. She had a house in Zagreb, and she thought that I had to go there, and whatever I had in my house was hers now. My house was new, built in 1980 or 1981. I had my own shop, well stocked with the goods that I had bought, unencumbered by a single dinar of loan. It was all mine. We had a piece of land that we bought for our eldest son, so that we could build a house for him, because our shop was a great success. She said that she had a house in Zagreb and a piece of land, and that we should go there; and whatever we had, and everything in our house was brand new, was going to become her property now. And in exchange, she lifted all the things that she had in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Was she Serb, Serbian?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: She was a Serb from Zagreb. She and her son came looking for a house, whereas her elder son was in the Serbian Army. She had two sons. The elder one was in the Serbian Army, the younger one was with her. And she had left her husband behind in Zagreb, in that house, so that --

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Excuse me. Did you try to call the police when this woman moved into your house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but they did not react in any way. On the contrary, they helped her. They were helping her, because since communications had broken down at the time, they were cut off, and they enabled her to talk to her husband in Zagreb. I remember well that at one point my aunt came, saw a police car outside the house. My aunt came in all frightened, and she said, "What happened in your house? Why is the police here?" I just shrugged my shoulders. I told her, "Well, you can see for yourself. One doesn't dare say anything." And since we had no choice, we packed our things. And how did we pack? We packed like gypsies.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: When she said that she had all that we needed in Zagreb, that we should exchange houses. That's when we packed. I'm telling you, she had been in our house for ten days up to that moment, and we realised we had no choice, because when a Serb comes into your house, you can say goodbye to it. You are left without anything in the world. There was only one man who managed to expel the new occupants, there was one single case, so we thought we'd better leave. And as I said, we packed. They gave us a few bags. We had an Opel Ascona, and we loaded it with all the things that would fit into the car and onto the roof. All the clothing and necessities we managed to put in the boot of the car, including some of my valuable zepter crockery and pots.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ferrara, you have eight minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: What happened when you were in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: When we arrived in Zagreb, this Mico, the lady's husband who had been left behind, had transferred the title to the house to his brother, so legally we had no house. That lady had taken over our house, and we were in the street. Then Mr. Spiric came. I was in tears now. Spiric asked me what had happened. I explained. And then that husband left. We were in the street. Our house was gone. One child was with us, one child was in a boarding school. And then Spiric suggested that he could go to Hrtkovci and find another alternative house for us. My husband gave him a lift. And when he saw our house, he asked Mile to swap houses with us, himself; and we agreed to that swap, although we were getting less. He only had the house, no land, nothing, but still we agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did you sign any contract for this exchange?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was all done legally. Our house has all the relevant documents; water certificates, urban certificates, everything. He didn't have anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, can we have on the screen the document with the 65 ter number 1398, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that has to do with the house exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Is this the contract you signed by Mr. Bilic -- with Mr. Spiric, sorry?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to admit into evidence the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's give it a number. Let's give this official contract a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be given Exhibit number P631. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe the condition of this house that you got in Zagreb, and the condition of the house that you left in Hrtkovci?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: In Hrtkovci, well, I have a photograph which you can have a look at to see what the house looked like. If you're interested in it, I can show it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we put it on the ELMO, this photo?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd just like to draw your attention to the fact that in similar cases, when the Defence wants to show something, the Prosecution is on its feet, but I have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's take a look at this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: What's this?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: The photograph shows my house, which I built in 1980 and 1981. There is a real cellar, and it's a real house with foundations.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to add this document to our exhibit list, and --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This photograph cannot be admitted into evidence until the Prosecution obtains a photograph of the house that Ms. Paulic is living in Zitnjak, in Zagreb right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But that was the exact question I was going to ask the witness. Do you have a picture of your house today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's like this: I have half a photograph, because it was an old house and the roof had to be replaced this year. I can switch my mobile phone on and show you part of the house that has been renovated. You can see the part that I renovated, you can see that it's new. This was done this year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ferrara, you represent the OTP. You knew very well that when you were asking to see this picture, inevitably we would want to see the picture of the house where the witness lives in now. But it seems that this photograph of her house, where she lives now, is on her mobile phone, so you should have done what was needed in order to have a hard copy of this picture, and you didn't do this. You just told us that she only had the photograph on her mobile phone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I, myself, said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The picture of the house you live in in Zagreb, is it only on your mobile phone? That's what I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can we see this photo?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But I didn't tell that to Prosecution. I have this for my own sake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me consult with my fellow Judges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber will not admit this picture, neither picture, neither one of them. Take your picture, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can you describe the condition of the house in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: The house was smaller. It was all covered in wallpaper on the inside. You know what wallpaper is. It doesn't have any foundations, windows -- when that wallpaper came unstuck, when we removed the wallpaper, tears started flowing. We were horrified. We renovated everything, literally everything. His son, Spiric's son, was there last year, his son who was in the Serbian army. He came to attend a neighbour's wedding. He wanted to take photographs of the inside. I said, "Feel free to do so." I said, "You can take photographs, but there's nothing for you to photograph. Everything has been renovated." Naturally, if you take the ugliest girl and dress her up as a bride, she'll be beautiful. Well, that's what that house looks like. But now that the roof caved in, well, I can describe the house for you. We buttressed the house up. Well, it's a bit like putting a lid on a pot. That's how the top caved in. So, very briefly, that's how I would describe it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: My last question: Did you exchange with Mr. Spiric only your house in Hrtkovci or also a piece of land, a piece of land as well? What did you give to Mr. Spiric?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: The house, the land. We had to give him everything in exchange for his house. And in addition, he asked for us to give him 800 German marks. At the time, one used marks, not Euros. We had to give him that money so that he could pay for a lorry to collect the things that he wanted, all the -- he said he wouldn't do this. He took his things, he packed them. We gave him 800 kuna, and he left without a word.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did you hear of other non-Serbs who exchanged their house with Serbs that lived outside Hrtkovci?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: You mean Hungarians, people who weren't Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I heard about that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Any of your relatives?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult for me to talk about that. My brother had a house, a house that was newer than mine. It was built of facade bricks. He had a small, orderly house. While Spiric was moving out, I went to Franjo's out of curiosity to see how he was, because I'm his sister and I feel for him. In the front rooms, they had left some earth. Why, I don't know. The house was in a terrible state, but at the time it was terrible. My sister-in-law was crying. I tried to console her. I'm quite courageous, as you can see. I'm courageous. I consoled her. I said, "Well, what's important is that you're alive and that your children are healthy. That's also the case with my children. You'll always have a house, you'll have everything." She couldn't reconcile herself to that for a certain period of time. Eventually she became reconciled to that. But the house and the yard and everything else was in a very bad state.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let me turn to my fellow Judges to see if they have any questions. Witness, I have just one question for you. In your testimony, there's just one thing I find relevant, and that is the speech given by Mr. Seselj. You said that he gave names. Apparently, Mr. Seselj did not know the names of the people whose name was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He didn't know them, but he had been provided with a list of those people. But it's true, he couldn't have known those people. He knew none of us, none of us. He didn't come to Hrtkovci to get to know the locals. He was a stranger for us. He wasn't a local inhabitant. He arrived in the village and created a disturbance, but he was given that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are saying that he was given a list. How do you know this? How do you come to that conclusion? Did someone tell you about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everyone said that -- what's his name -- Ostoja Sibincic had compiled the list and recorded the houses, so the numbers of the houses and the names of the streets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Ostoja Sibincic is the one who compiled the list and gave it to Mr. Seselj; and Mr. Seselj, when he delivered his speech, read out the list and the names. And you mentioned the name of your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was Mr. Sibincic on bad terms with your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, he acted as if he wasn't in a conflict with anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Earlier on, we saw the picture of your house. It's a nice house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For me, a beautiful house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, Mr. Sibincic could have put your name on the list. Why is it that he didn't do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't know why he didn't do that. Perhaps he was afraid of my husband. My husband is quite a strict man, and they'd been down there together because he worked for the local commune. As for his reasons, well, I don't know. I, myself, am surprised by this. I apologise. It's probably because he no longer worked in the local commune, but worked for me. So he wasn't making a post vacant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case, you are saying that you are certain that it's Mr. Seselj who gave these names; you're 100 per cent sure about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those names were quite clearly pronounced. I know that because I know all those people, and I was horrified by what I heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And those names were pronounced by Mr. Seselj or by someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He uttered the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. So you are quite sure about this. Mr. Seselj, please proceed with your cross-examination. You have one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Ms. Paulic, before your testimony today, had you prepared your testimony with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: A little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the course of that proofing, did you go through the statement that you signed a long time ago?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm familiar with it. I'll never forget it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm not asking you whether you are familiar with it, but whether you and a representative of the OTP went through the text.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In that case, why didn't you tell the Prosecution many of the things that you have first stated today?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, I could go into that, but you'd need a 500- or 600-page book.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, why didn't you write that book, then?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You're not the sort that the Prosecution wants to obtain information from in advance. You want to surprise the Prosecution in the courtroom as well?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, I was asked a few questions and I answered them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And now you've felt free to talk about things you weren't asked about?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. Let's go and deal with these things in order. Before coming to The Hague, did you speak to the Croatian authorities?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can you look at me when I ask you questions?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Be courteous, then. I'm looking at you. I'd like you to look at me.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I can look at you, but I don't see why.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If I'm putting a question to you and if you're answering my question, well, then it would be decent for us to look at each other.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: The Judges are here to be looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But when the accused puts questions to you, then you are engaging in a dialogue with the accused.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I can hear the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You can hear me sufficiently well, so you don't need to look at me. Don't you feel uneasy? Is your conscience ill at ease, and as a result you can't look me in the eyes?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, then you don't want to look me in the eyes out of spite, not because you can't?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Why should I want to look at you. You are such an evil man.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you've never seen a more handsome man, never in your life.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, whatever you say. That's a well-known fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. You don't want to look me in the eyes. What can I do about it? I'm looking in your eyes. Why did you invent the story about Slavko Mirazic, saying that he was a member of the Serbian Radical Party, where that was never the case? He is not a member of that party today, either.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't invent that. That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He was a member of the Serbian Renewal Movement, and everyone in Hrtkovci knew that and that's probably the case today because no one is aware of him having left that body.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: That's his problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. If that's his problem, if it's his problem that you accuse him of being a member of the Serbian Radical Party. You said that the refugees in Hrtkovci started arriving from various parts of Croatia as early as 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Most of them came after the fall of many places in Western Slavonia in December 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: They were continually arriving.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But most of them came from Grubisno Polje, Slatina, and some other places. Can you remember the names of those places?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Grubisno Polje, I remember that place; and I also remember Kule.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You mentioned the case or a case that isn't referred to in your statement. You said that there was an old lady living alone in your neighbourhood, in a good house, in a nice house. Her son was abroad. The lady died. The son sold the house, and then some refugees illegally moved into the house. The new owner arrived, and he couldn't get them to leave. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: The new owner bought the house, and then they arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I interpreted what you said. Refugees moved in. When he heard about that, he came from abroad, he tried to expel them; and he was unsuccessful. I'm interested in the name of the old lady who died. You didn't mention it.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: The old lady, Kata Francuz.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What was her surname?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Francuz, Kata Francuz.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What was her son's name?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, how do I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How don't you know the name of neighbour's son? You would see the old lady, Kata, every day; and she would continually speak to you about her son, if what you're saying is the truth, because you needed some time to remember the name of the old lady. I haven't heard about that surname, Francuz, in Hrtkovci, but I'll check on this when you leave. What was the name of the new owner when he bought the house from the old lady Kata's son?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I wasn't interested in his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Partially, to an extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why didn't you mention this fact to the Prosecution when you spoke to the Prosecution the first time? It's a very interesting case. The old lady, Kata, died. The son sold the house. Refugees moved in. Why didn't you tell the Prosecution about this? Didn't they ask you about it?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, what then?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't ask me about this. I said there were so many cases -- there was so many cases, I could write a book about it. You can't remember everything, but I just remembered that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you also needed a little time to remember the name of old lady Kata?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. You said that the refugees arrived and that they moved around town in groups of four, five, or six individuals; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who did these refugees attack?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: They attacked good houses. They wouldn't attack poor people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How did they attack? Did they form groups, then have artillery fire, then mortars? Did they then fire shots? What did the attack look like, or did they just appear, knock on doors, say, "We're from such-and-such a place, we have a good house. Would you like us to do an exchange"? What did this attack resemble?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: There was no knocking. They would enter the yards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, when you enter a yard, do you have to knock?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: It depends.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, what do you knock on when you enter a yard?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Sir, you knock on the door, but let me repeat this. It depended. They entered the yards. They made threats, used bad language, disturbed us and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Perhaps that happened on occasion. I believe that is the case. But you don't have any specific information, you're inventing things, and you're talking in general terms.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, dear Seselj, I know about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you're afraid to look me in the eyes, and I can see that you're not telling the truth. That's quite sufficient for me.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, look --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Shall we use the "T" form of addressing each other, the impolite form of addressing each other?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. We have a technical problem here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, please, do not ask that question again to the witness about why the witness is not looking at you. When the witness was answering the questions of Mr. Ferrara, she was looking at the Judges. Everybody's free to look at the Judges.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Lattanzi, according to procedural law, in direct testimony is one of the main principles, that the testimony has to appear in person and address the court, and this is one of the basic factors for checking the witness' credibility. And then there is the witness' body language. A truthful witness looks the person putting questions to the witness in the eyes. As a student at the faculty of law, this is something that I was taught. It's part of criminal law. I won't go on about this, but on two occasions I informed you of how I interpret this, and you can draw the conclusions you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. How did they threaten you? Apart from the phone calls, which we can't check up on - who knows whether there were any such phone calls or not - but did anyone curse you, for example, in the street?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, if they were my friends, well, was it only a matter of cursing --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. There wasn't any swearing.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, there were all sorts of things, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I want to clarify this. Were there any swear words used, and which ones?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, we're not going to start cursing, using swear words in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No, we won't, but we'll tell the Chamber what sort of swear words were used.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Is it that important? It's so ugly, should I have to tell you that they cursed my mother, that they cursed my child or, rather, they said that my child was a member of the ZNG, the Home Guards Corps. All sorts of words were used. It's not important.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm drawing a conclusion from the fact that you don't want to say which swear words were used. Well, finally you said that they cursed your mother, so the conclusion I draw is that no one used any swear words; and when you imagine such things, when you invent such things, you're not finding your bearing in this cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Sir, I don't use swear words. I don't want to do so. I'm a Catholic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm not interested in the fact that you're a Catholic, and I didn't say that you used swear words. What I want to say is that in Hrtkovci, you're well known as a person who can be quite brazen and people don't really want to have a verbal conflict with you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on. You said a certain Jovo brought in some people who wanted to enter your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You don't know what this Jovo's surname is?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is he a refugee or a local inhabitant?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Jovo is a refugee. He has a house, together with his brother, in Zagreb, in a neighbourhood called Zitnjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did this Jovo incite you to go there to Zitnjak and to do some sightseeing and find someone to possibly swap houses with? You are hesitating for a long time. What's the reason?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: And you are nervous, aren't you? Jovo finally admitted to me this: "I am bringing to you other people all the time, but I have a house myself in Zagreb, in Zitnjak, that you could take in exchange for your house."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did Jovo introduce you to Dragutin Spiric, with whom you swapped houses?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to know. Now, let's come to the rally. Why were you astounded by the broadcasting of Serb songs before the rally? You don't like Serbian songs?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you were taken aback?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I was taken aback because I had never heard any of them before that moment, and it sounded horrible to me. Why would Seselj's arrival necessarily mean that these songs would be booming around town?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What else would you play before a rally?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, I listened to other songs. They were very nice songs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You mean songs about Ban Jelacic, young Ustashas charging into battle. But, anyway, every bird flies to his own nest. Some are even willing to sacrifice themselves for their own flock.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Let it be.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You saw, at my rally, you say, men dressed in black from head to toe, with ammunition belts on their chests and terrible cockades on their hats. What's so terrible about those cockades?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: What was terrible? Well, it was terrifying to me, because I had never seen them before. How wouldn't it be? What were suddenly Serbian soldiers doing in our beautiful, peaceful village?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You say in your statement there was very few police at the rally; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And we have information from a man who worked in the State Security Service, Slavko Kolundzic, who attended the rally as part of his job; and he said there was a lot of police security and you didn't see it?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It seemed to you that those policemen were Seselj's soldiers, with ammunition belts and Serbian-style hats?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You say that these cockades were as big as plates?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: That there are all sorts of sizes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It says here that "they were as big as plates."

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: That's how things looked like when you are frightened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And these hats, were they as big as army caldrons? If the cockades were as big as plates, then the hats had to be as big as army caldrons; right?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I don't know the size of an army caldron. I've never been in the army. But they were black and pointed, ugly. Again, I'm saying I've never seen them before.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So even the hats were ugly to you?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were pointed and ugly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, these Serbian-style hats were produced as Serbian military uniform in the 19th century, emulating French hats, and the Serbian military uniform in the First World War was among the most beautiful army uniforms. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: We didn't want to know about that. We liked our traditional national costumes of the Sokac people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You mean Sokac, Serbs who converted to Catholicism?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, they used to be Orthodox and then they converted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, I learned about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You mean from your own books? Why do you keep saying that Hungarians were mentioned at the rally, when nobody ever mentioned Hungarians?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Sir, I am not making anything up. I did not come here to make things up. I came here to tell the truth and only the truth. And you, if you were proud enough to pound your chest there, be brave here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I am, I am brave. There's nobody braver in the whole Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Fine. During that speech, did I say that all children from mixed marriages should be killed?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I've been warned by interpreters to make a pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What are you looking at? Is somebody sending you any messages?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Come and see, come and have a look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you can look at the screen, but at the screen what you see is the English translation of your answers or of Mr. Seselj's questions, or the Judges' questions. If you like to learn English, you can do so, but maybe at another time. Now, could you please answer Mr. Seselj's questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Will you answer my question? Please try. Did I say at that meeting that all children from mixed marriages should be killed off?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I heard with my own ears that you said mixed marriages should be broken.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And children killed?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything about children, because as you said, I am very talkative myself and Milena was standing next to me, a child of a mixed marriage; and it didn't hurt me so much because of Milena but because of my own sister who is in a mixed marriage and has two children, so I started talking to her immediately. I didn't hear about children, but you did say that mixed marriages between Croats and Serbs should be broken up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And who was at that rally from your own family?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't have to tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You do have to tell me.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: My niece. There were others, but she is the most important.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was your brother there?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: My brother lives on one end, I live on another. I repeat to you that I was on the street where my house is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And how many people attended that rally?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: About a thousand, give or take.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So was your brother at the rally or not? Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Can you really see every face in such a big crowd? I believe he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was he or wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I believe he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you talk to your brother at any time after the rally about the things you heard?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: The whole village talked, not just my brother and I. Everybody talked about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 12.00, and I believe we should break for 20 minutes. We'll resume at 12.20. We'll finish at 1.15. I think you have used up 25 minutes already, you'll have 35 minutes left, so normally we shall be able to finish on time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court is back in session. Mr. Seselj, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Ms. Paulic, you said at one point that in my speech at that rally, I read a list of names. How come that I, as the president of a political party coming to a rally, read a list of names of inhabitants of Hrtkovci who should be expelled? Doesn't that sound tragic comic to you, ridiculous? It's my electoral campaign. I'm making a political speech, making promises as to what the Serbian Radical Party would do when they come into power; and I also advocate the principle of retorsion, that is, an exchange of population of Croatia, saying that if Croatia expelled so many Serbs, we would do the same to Croats, briefly we would do to Croats whatever the Tudjman regime did to Serbs. And then I take out a list of inhabitants of Hrtkovci and read it out? Isn't that a bit ridiculous? Shall I have to wait much longer? The interpretation has finished long ago.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: It was funny to us at the time, but obviously, looking at you, it wasn't funny. You did it all in a politically-organised way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: First, we expelled hundreds of thousands of Serbs from Croatia, and then we expelled a couple of thousand Croats from Serbia. It was all conceived and designed by us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, would it be possible to turn off the screen in front of Ms. Paulic, where she's following the transcript, so that she can think about answers, because the transcript lags behind the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Witness, don't waste your time looking at the screen. I don't know what you're looking at. Maybe you see myself on the screen, and then there's another screen with text in English that is scrolling. But it's useless for you, unless you need time to think about your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not impossible that somebody is sending her answers to my questions. This waiting is very suspicious.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nobody needs to send me answers. I can easily answer to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So when I get your goat a little, then you're very ready to answer. So let me go on. How do you know -- where did you get this idea that Ostoja Sibincic gave me that list to read?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, who else would it be? He was the main organiser in Hrtkovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And to what party did Ostoja Sibincic belong to at the time?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: You know that well. Why would you ask me if you know it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I know very well. I'm asking you, as a witness.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Just like you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You mean he was a member of the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you sure.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, if you're sure, why would we go on. You said that you were in Hrtkovci when the wife of Dragutin Spiric came and came into your house with her child?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Not Spiric's wife, another woman with whom we were supposed to swap houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you didn't, eventually?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Not with that woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Because her house was not good enough for you?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No. The thing is that her husband, while she was staying in my house, signed over the title to the house to his brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you went to Zitnjak in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: The surname is Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Wait a little. So you personally went to Zitnjak, near Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: She invited us with the intention to swap house for house, Mico Milutinovic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And since your agreement with the Milutinovic's fell through?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: That's not how it happened. We went to the registrar, to the public notary, and the public notary found that there were no papers, no title.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then you went around and made inquiries around Zitnjak?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No. I was sitting down and crying when Dragutin Spiric came in and asked me why I was crying. And I answered, to which he said, "Dear lady, come and have a look at my house." So I did go because it was nearby. My husband went back to Hrtkovci because we realised we had lost our house, there was no title to the other house. We had a shop and a house, and Spiric told my husband to find another house in Hrtkovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You've told us all that. Zitnjak is a neighbourhood in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Four kilometres from the center?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: That's not true. It's seven or eight kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I have a statement here --

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, that's your problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You are quite quarrelsome now. That's better. The wife of Dragutin Spiric says it's four kilometres from the center of Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Let it be.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It was populated by 70 per cent Serbs before the war?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: How would I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were there many Serbs? You live there now.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I know about now, but I don't know about before.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's right. You did not count them as they were leaving, did you? The wife of Dragutin Spiric says that you came and went around the neighbourhood, looking for a house that would be suitable, and you viewed a lot of Serbian houses. And that was not unusual in any way, because many Croats had come before and after you to look at Serb houses and inquire about possible swapping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ferrara.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Yes, I did not understand. Mr. Seselj is reading a statement of the wife of Dragutin Spiric? It was never disclosed to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I understood, too. But you know that --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the Prosecutor has no idea what has or hasn't been disclosed to him. This -- in fact, to me. This is in my book, "The Hrtkovci Scandal," and if I give you some headlines, you are again going to redact it from the transcript and turn it into a private session. So there's "The Hrtkovci Affair," in the headline and a few more words. I disclosed it to the Prosecution in good time, at least a month before the first Hrtkovci witness appeared, and the Prosecutor should do his homework.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ferrara, this statement made by this woman is in the book that you received.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Maybe Mr. Seselj should point out before reading and say, "I'm reading a statement in the book," and so on. Of course, we have thousands of documents. We cannot know everything in the documents. He should be more precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this book, (redacted) (redacted) and so on, consists of studies on the Hrtkovci case, written by my associates, that I had turned over to you in October of last year with my objection to the indictment. You decided at the time that it shouldn't be translated into English. You only translated the objection and ruled on the objection. If you had translated it all into English, I believe that the evidence on Hrtkovci would have been so convincing that you would have, without any hesitation, decided to remove all references to Hrtkovci in the indictment. So this is the study in my book, first, and then goes all the rest; the judgements, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Please continue the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It's mostly finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. If I'm not mistaken, Mr. Seselj, the Chamber ruled that you could have a great number of pages translated into English. So far, we haven't seen one single page. Because you have not ordered it or why?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I told you last time that this is probably a very interesting book, as far as what happened in this municipality is concerned, so you should have thought about the fact that the Judges needed to know about this book. When this book was mentioned ages ago, we had no idea what was in the book, and now I'm discovering that in this book we could find the statement made by this woman, this woman who was part of the exchange of houses. It's quite interesting. So out of the 10.000 pages in the book, you should have told the translation department, "Translate this page and that page so that the Judges know about these elements." But this is something you did not do. I note that this book might be of interest, but unfortunately we don't have it, it's not available to us. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Two points, very quickly. As we've indicated in the past, the book primarily consists of material that is -- that relates to protected witnesses or material that the Trial Chamber has ordered to be placed under seal. Second of all, the book is more than a thousand pages' long, and we would ask the Trial Chamber to order the accused that when he is going to be using parts of that book, or any of his other books, in terms of cross-examination, that he needs to notify us so that we can have those parts of the book ready and available to us. Simply saying he's disclosed a 1.000-page book to us, and, therefore, anything and everything in it is fair game for each and every witnesses in cross-examination, is not fair; and we need notification, just as the Trial Chamber does, so that Your Honours can have those pages before you when he cross-examines a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Mundis. You know that the events linked to this municipality are very important, of paramount importance to this document, notably because of the speech that was made there and everything that occurred around the speech. And because of this, the OTP must know of all of the book, the entire book. If I were you, I would know the book from page 1 to the last page. If the accused is talking about this book, then the OTP would have the answer, if the OTP knew the book. I know that you came in, in midstream, you know, and you were not able to know of all the exhibits, but when you're a prosecutor, and it's a job I had at one point, it's to know everything, to know all the evidence, to be aware of the existence of the entire body of evidence so that you're never taken by surprise by the Defence. If he is mentioning part of a book, normally you should be able to answer quickly without having to be told about the page where the passage can be found. If I had read this book, I could tell you by route, you know, the page and the paragraph. Unfortunately, we're not given this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with all due respect, the fact that the witness -- or the fact that the accused wants to cross-examine from certain pages of the book is certainly something that he can notify us about in advance. The fact is, as we've said before, this book contains largely information that shouldn't have been published and put into the public domain in the first place. The remainder of that book, if the accused knows he's going to cross-examine on certain parts of the book, he has an obligation, just as any other accused or any other Defence team do, to provide adequate notice to us so that we can be thoroughly prepared. This is what is known as trial by ambush, and it is no more fair to the Prosecution to allow this to proceed than it would be if we were to try the same thing against the accused. It's a fundamental issue of equality of arms. And I note for the record, once again, Dr. Seselj is laughing. This is inappropriate behaviour in the courtroom, and we would ask again, these are exactly the kinds of things that demand imposition of counsel immediately. We are not getting a fair trial, we're not being put on fair notice as to what he's cross-examining on, and when I raise issues, he mocks us. This is not the way to proceed, with all due respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I was not looking at you. You are not supposed to smirk or smile when the Prosecutor is talking. And Mr. Mundis is right in one part. If, in this book, there are passages on protected witnesses, you must be very careful and never mention this in open session. However, this was not the case, because our witness here is not protected, and the wife -- everything that deals with the wife of the person who swapped -- they swapped apartments with is not protected either. But we now have some minutes left, and you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, first of all, laughter is something that one can often not control. It's a spontaneous reaction of an individual to certain events. It can be controlled sometimes, but not always, and it cannot be forbidden. First of all, I did not laugh out loud, and thus it was not insulting, it was not offensive. I have disclosed this book to the Prosecution, and I meant to submit one copy for translation. But when I saw that you forbade the title to be mentioned in the courtroom, I gave up on that idea. Third, I wasn't quoting from the book. I am interpreting part of the statement of Dragutin Spiric's wife. I didn't even have time to write down her name, so I keep referring to her as Dragutin Spiric's wife. And it is only after the intervention of the Prosecutor that I said that it was published -- that statement was published in the book. I have the right to use it in my cross-examination. Fourth, Mr. President, I am, in principle, opposing that any statement taken by the Defence or the Prosecution be admitted into evidence without prior cross-examination, just as I oppose the proffering by the Prosecutor of 92 ter statements that the Prosecutor, himself, has written, and that's why I did not offer into evidence -- I did not tender the statements -- witness statements taken by my own associates. When I call Defence statements, I will bring many of those who have already given written statements. But that's something we can leave for later. I have the right to interpret various statements, and if the Prosecutor asks me, I'll tell him it comes from a book. They can find it. It says, in Dragutin Spiric's wife's statement, that Ms. Paulic came to Zitnjak, looked around for a suitable house for purposes of an exchange, and now I'm putting it to her that Dragutin Spiric's wife claims that the Spiric family had swapped their house in a blind exchange for the Paulics' house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, the contract on the exchange was drafted by Igor Kanajet, attorney-at-law; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: From another village, and it was verified in Zagreb. That attorney is from Dugo Selo. That's just outside Zagreb; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So, you see, I know a few things myself, and Dugo Selo is not in Ruma municipality where the Hrtkovci is. And now I'm asking the witness: You and your husband intended to cheat Dragutin Spiric and his wife, and in concluding that contract, they did not provide all the necessary documentation. So when Dragutin Spiric came to Hrtkovci, he could not book the house in Hrtkovci in his own name; whereas the Paulics signed in the register, in the land register, immediately. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No, no, we couldn't transfer the title. We couldn't have transferred the title unless it was all legal. Everything was legal. We had all the permits, all the papers. There was no encumbering mortgages or anything, loans.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Ms. Paulic, you didn't give Dragutin Spiric all the necessary documents. Your house was legal.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: How could we have transferred it, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: With the help of the documents in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And Dragutin Spiric didn't have all the necessary documents to register it in Ruma?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: How could he have sold it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: First he filed charges against you?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpreters are complaining. Witness, you must wait for Mr. Seselj to be finished with his question before answering, as it takes some time, but don't take too long. And try not to answer too fast. Otherwise, the interpreters cannot keep track of what you are saying. Continue, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, can we see a document from the Prosecution binder, one that the Prosecution didn't want to use for some reason. The Prosecution provided me the document evidence according to which Dragutin Spiric filed charges against you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Ms. Paulic, did you cheat him?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He didn't file charges against you?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the documents weren't in order, we wouldn't have been able to sell the house immediately and we wouldn't have been able to open an establishment, a catering establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He didn't do anything, but he prosecuted you.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: How could I have sold the house if the documents weren't in order?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you did the exchange in Zagreb, you did not give Dragutin Spiric all the necessary documents.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: It wasn't necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It wasn't necessary because you wanted to cheat him?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then Dragutin Spiric arrived in Hrtkovci. He was first astounded because he had been given a house that wasn't as good as the one he had, according to his wife. He also suffered a stroke shortly after that. The house was empty, it wasn't furnished, there was nothing in it, whereas he had left you all his property in the house in Zitnjak?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Were you listening to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Did you listen to what I said in my statement? I said Spiric went to have a look at a different house in Hrtkovci with my husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That has nothing to do with what I'm asking you about.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does. Listen to me. He saw my house. He brought a photograph of my house with him and showed it to the lady. You said that she was shedding tears, apparently, and complaining. Well, she said the following, "Is it possible for us to actually get that house?" And they told us that they had to go so that the children could be together, because their son was in the Serbian army, in your army. He left the army to go to the Serbian army and his daughter stayed in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did he wear a cockade hat?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Have a look at this document. It's a judgement from the Ruma Municipal Court, issued because you and your husband didn't respond to the charges.

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: We didn't receive it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It came into force on the 5th of October, 1993, and it states the following: "In the name of the people, the Municipal Court in Ruma, the court of first instance in this litigation with Judge Dragan Mandic as president of the Chamber, and illegal matter of Dragutin Spiric from Hrtkovci, represented by Mladen Grbic, a lawyer from Ruma, against Defendants Mile Paulic and Katica Paulic from Zagreb. "With the purpose of establishment of facts, during the preliminary hearing, the first hearing before the main hearing on the 16th of July, 1993, in the presence of the proxor [phoen] of the plaintiff, in absence of the defence, who have been summoned, delivered the following." So the verdict for the failure to appear is as follows: "It has been established that the plaintiff, Dragutin Spiric from Hrtkovci, is the owner of property registered in Land Registry Hrtkovci under number 1972; namely, the parcel number 15281, which is land consisting of four areas," and so forth. "The defendants are obliged to admit to the said and to issue a tabulation fit to re-register the said property from the names." You didn't want to issue him with that document so that he could register the property. That's how you cheated him?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He had to consult the courts, refer the matter to the courts?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: He wanted to sell the property. He did so. That was his intention, and that's it. Had we cheated him? Well, no, we didn't cheat him. We didn't receive this document, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Just pause there, please. It says you should have given him the document so that he could register the property in the name of the person filing the charges. It says: "This verdict shall substitute for any opposite conduct on this issue within 15 days, with the possibility of enforcement." So Mr. Spiric had to go to court to prove that he had exchanged houses with you. And on the basis of the court judgement, he had to register his house in his name, because you didn't give him the documents he needed to register the house. He provided you, however, with all the documents you needed, and you had no problems to register the house in Zagreb in your name. Is that what this judgement, in fact, shows?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Well, I'll repeat what I said. We didn't receive this judgement, and I'll repeat what I said. There was no reason for him to file such charges, because all our documents were in order.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In that case, why would he file such charges, if there was no reason?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: You have to ask him that question. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why would the Court issue a judgement if all the documents were available? Are you a little surprised by this judgement?

utterances.speaker: KATICA PAULIC
utterances.text: Yes, naturally.
